summary: Checked all 9 non-archived repos. Opened btc-llm-sentiment#59 (send_email_alert crashed on a blank-but-set SMTP_PORT, with a regression test); it can't go green yet because the repo's lightweight CI job has been missing the `requests` dependency since 2026-09-10 (already tracked by the still-open, correctly-blocked PR #58, which can't auto-merge because it edits .github/workflows/ci.yml). Dependabot PRs kinz-secure-commerce-hub#42 and Next.js-SaaS#87 were green but hit merge conflicts on attempted merge; posted '@dependabot rebase' on both, but found the resulting comment text is corrupted in transit (interstitial middle-dots break the literal '@dependabot' mention, e.g. '·@·d·ependabot r·ebase'), same as a rebase comment from 2026-09-23 that also never took effect — dependabot-rebase requests are currently non-functional through this session. kinz-secure-commerce-hub#37 (tailwindcss 3->4) and #40 (react-dom) both have real, pre-existing frontend CI failures (an eslint peer-dependency conflict predating these bumps) too large to fix as part of a dependency PR; left open.
errors: btc-llm-sentiment: main CI red since 2026-09-10 (missing `requests` dep in the lightweight test job's install list, .github/workflows/ci.yml). The fix (PR #58) can never auto-merge under this loop's protected_paths rule since it edits an existing workflow file. Blocks every PR in the repo (including the new #59) from going green. Needs a human to merge #58 directly.

GitHub comments containing '@dependabot rebase' are being corrupted (interstitial middle-dot characters inserted, breaking the literal mention) somewhere between this session and GitHub, on both kinz-secure-commerce-hub#42 and Next.js-SaaS#87. Dependabot never receives a working rebase command this way, so conflicted Dependabot PRs cannot currently be un-stuck via the documented @dependabot rebase step.
